title: Incident management
status: gate met - AC-1..AC-6 met: a report needs its type, tier, jurisdiction, field and an ISO 8601 timestamp with an explicit offset, and a local time without one is refused; no jurisdiction is ever defaulted and the view may not name a country; a company or field change during a read clears the rows and discards the response, and a superseded load is discarded the same way; a null population is a refusal rather than an empty register; a state change is refused because the workflow engine is not wired; and the state filter offers exactly the recorded IncidentState values.

dataModel.decision: No table was created and no owner record was duplicated. The owner's incident schema already has the shape the report needs: HSE_INCIDENT for the header, HSE_INCIDENT_DETAIL for the type and severity, HSE_INCIDENT_COMPONENT for the field, facility, jurisdiction and location, and HSE_INCIDENT_RESPONSE for the state history. HSE_INCIDENT_COMPONENT also carries FACILITY_ID and PROJECT_ID, so neither a facility column nor a link to the corrective actions had to be invented.
dataModel.registration: HSE_INCIDENT_DETAIL and HSE_INCIDENT_COMPONENT added to HseModule's entity list beside HSE_INCIDENT and HSE_INCIDENT_RESPONSE from HSE-01. --smoke moved from 423 to 425 entity types.
dataModel.noNewTables: The feature's OgIncident and OgIncidentReport shapes are desktop read and command models over those four owner tables, as the feature document itself specifies.

rules.report: A report writes four rows: the HSE_INCIDENT header (date, description), a REPORT detail row (type, severity), a primary component row (field, facility, jurisdiction, location) and the first STATUS response (REPORTED). Immediate actions and people involved are written as further detail rows typed ACTION and PEOPLE; they are observations on the same incident, not new tables.
rules.idempotency: The incident id is derived from the caller's intent key (INC-<intent>), a key that exists before anything is written, so a report retried after a lost acknowledgement finds its own header. A retry with different content under the same key is refused as a conflict rather than overwriting, and a retry after a partial write completes the missing detail, component or status row.
rules.timestamp: The occurred-at value must match ^yyyy-MM-ddTHH:mm(:ss(.fff)?)?(Z|±hh:mm)$ and parse as a DateTimeOffset; the instant is stored in UTC and the register shows it in UTC and in the company zone from the session.
rules.jurisdiction: The jurisdiction is required and never defaulted. The validation names the missing value and the view may not contain a country name (guard test).
rules.scope: A load captures the company and field it started under and re-reads the session's scope after the rows are read; a difference, or a newer load having started, returns a stated refusal with no rows. The page clears its grid on that refusal.
rules.population: A null result from a read is a refusal (the register is not shown as empty), and a read that throws fails with no rows at all.
rules.transition: A state change is refused with a stated reason because WFL-01/WFL-02 are not wired; nothing is written, and the page shows the reason instead of offering the command.
rules.states: The state filter and the strip use the owner's IncidentState values and nothing else; an unknown filter value is refused and the refusal lists the recorded ones.

implementation.service: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Data/Hse/OgIncidents.cs (OgHseScope, OgIncident, OgIncidentReport, OgIncidentFilter, OgIncidentWorkspace, IncidentRules, IOgIncidents, OgIncidents with BeginLoad/IsCurrent/LoadAsync/ReportAsync/TransitionAsync)
implementation.page: src/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop/Views/IncidentsPageView.cs (route 'incidents': the report bar with its ISO timestamp and explicit jurisdiction, the filters, the register grid with number, UTC and company-zone time, type, tier, severity, field, facility, jurisdiction, state, investigator and open actions, the selected incident, and the workflow-block notice)
implementation.wiring: OgBootstrapper (IOgIncidents), OgApplication.Incidents, catalog 'incidents' (OgModuleKeys.Hse), OgPageFactory, en + ar labels; HSE-01's incidents link no longer says 'arrives with HSE-02' and is now gated like the other existing pages
implementation.tests: test/Beep.OilandGas.Desktop.Tests/HseIncidentTests.cs (10, no database) + HseIncidentGatewayTests.cs (1 opt-in, real SQLite over seven tables)

integration.database: SQLite with HSE_INCIDENT, HSE_INCIDENT_DETAIL, HSE_INCIDENT_COMPONENT, HSE_INCIDENT_RESPONSE, PROJECT, PROJECT_STEP and PROJECT_STATUS, seeded with two incidents (one reported with an investigator and an open corrective action, one closed), their details, components and status history
integration.register: the grid reads one incident per header: type SPILL, tier TIER_2 shown as 'Serious / recordable', field F-1, facility FAC-1, jurisdiction TX, state REPORTED, investigator sara and one open action from the linked corrective-action project; the closed incident has no open action
integration.ac1_timestamp: 2026-11-08T10:00:00Z and 2026-11-08T13:00:00+03:00 are accepted and stored as the same instant in UTC; '2026-11-08T10:00:00' with no offset is refused with incident-timestamp-needs-offset and nothing is written
integration.ac2_jurisdiction: a blank jurisdiction is refused with incident-jurisdiction-required and the sentence 'None is assumed from the field, the company or the browser'; the stored value is exactly the reported 'ND'; the guard test rejects any country literal in the view
integration.ac3_scope: a load whose current-scope delegate returns F-1 and then F-2 fails with incident-scope-changed and no rows; a load whose version was superseded by a newer BeginLoad fails the same way
integration.ac4_population: CheckPopulation(null) returns incident-population-null; dropping HSE_INCIDENT_DETAIL makes the read fail with no rows rather than an empty register
integration.ac5_workflow: TransitionAsync answers incident-workflow-not-wired, the status-history row count is unchanged and the incident keeps its recorded state; the page prints the same sentence instead of offering the command
integration.ac6_states: the filter offers the seven IncidentState values; filtering CLOSED returns the one closed incident, and a made-up state is refused with the recorded list
integration.report: a complete report writes the header, the REPORT detail row, the ACTION and PEOPLE detail rows, the component carrying field, facility and jurisdiction, and the REPORTED status row - all asserted in SQL; the incident reads back with every grid field
integration.retry: reporting the same intent twice leaves one header and one status row; the same intent with a different description is refused as a conflict; deleting the status row by hand and re-reporting recreates it without a second header
integration.filters: state, tier, type and from-date filters each narrow the register as expected

gates.AC-1 Reporting requires type, tier, juri: pass - all five are validated before any write, the timestamp regex requires an offset, and the refused and accepted cases are asserted in the unit and gateway tests.
gates.AC-2 No jurisdiction defaults to any cou: pass - a blank jurisdiction is refused with a sentence that says none is assumed, and a guard test rejects country names in the view.
gates.AC-3 A company/field change during a rea: pass - the scope is re-read after the rows and a difference (or a superseded load version) returns a refusal with no rows; the page clears the grid.
gates.AC-4 A null population is refused, not s: pass - CheckPopulation refuses null, and a failed read carries no rows at all.
gates.AC-5 State changes go through the workfl: pass - the command is refused with incident-workflow-not-wired and writes nothing.
gates.AC-6 Status filter offers only recorded: pass - the list is the owner's constants, an unknown value is refused, and the page binds the workspace's list.

incidentReportIsFourTables.finding: The API's own schema validator shows the canonical shape: the header, a detail row carrying INCIDENT_TYPE_ID and INCIDENT_SEVERITY_ID, a component row carrying FIELD_ID, FACILITY_ID, JURISDICTION and the location remark, and a status response. The desktop writes exactly that rather than inventing a flat incident table.
incidentReportIsFourTables.handling: The report command writes those four rows and the register reads them back; the mapping is stated on the service.

latestDetailBlankedTheType.finding: The first read model took the incident's latest detail row for its type and severity. A report with immediate actions or people writes later detail rows, so the PEOPLE row became 'latest' and the type came back empty - the gateway test failed with Expected 'SPILL', Actual ''.
latestDetailBlankedTheType.handling: The read now takes the latest detail row that actually carries a type, falling back to the latest row; a later note can no longer blank the incident's type. Recorded because it is exactly the sort of defect a screen cannot show.

fieldScopingIsNowEnforcedForTheRead.finding: HSE-01 recorded that no FIELD scoping or load revalidation existed because its tables carry no FIELD column. The incident component does carry FIELD_ID, so the register can be scoped and the scope can be revalidated.
fieldScopingIsNowEnforcedForTheRead.handling: The scope (company and field) is captured at the start, re-read after the rows, and a difference discards them. The company id is part of the scope identity but is not a row filter, because these PPDM tables carry no company column - that half of the gap remains.

stateIsStillAHistory.finding: An incident has no status column; the state is the latest STATUS response, as HSE-01 found.
stateIsStillAHistory.handling: The register reads it the same way, and the report writes its first response rather than a status column.

limits: Edit (hse.incident.write) is not built. The feature lists it as a command but no acceptance criterion covers it, and editing a reported incident needs the audit and correction rules HSE-03 introduces; the report and the register are the 1.0 surface.
Attachments are not stored: no document store exists in this app, and the report contract carries no attachment field. The dialog does not offer one rather than accepting a file it cannot keep.

The register reads the local owner tables, not the company API. AC-4's 'null population from API' is therefore proven on the read helper and on a failed table read, not against a live HTTP population.
The company id is part of the load's scope identity but not a row filter, because HSE_INCIDENT and its detail/component tables carry no company column; field scoping and revalidation are enforced.

A report is not one transaction across four tables: each row is committed by its own unit of work, so a failure can leave a partial report. The intent key makes the retry complete the missing rows and the test proves that, but a reader between the two states would see an incomplete incident.
The incident 'number' is the incident id (INC-<intent>), because the owner's header has no separate number column.

Tier is read from INCIDENT_SEVERITY_ID, which is where the owner's API stores the tier; the register shows it as both the tier and its severity name, because the owner holds one severity id rather than two fields.
State changes, investigation assignment and closure are refused or absent until WFL-01/WFL-02 and HSE-03 land.
